thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated GPU OOMs and kernel errors on inference-pool-us-west. Auto-ticket INC-2002 created. Symptoms: rising 500s, container flaps, and CUDA illegal memory access traces since ~11:10 UTC.

maya_oncall: I'm taking the page. Initial look: multiple pods on node node-gpu-07 failing with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS during model shard load. Collecting logs now.

harry_runtime: excerpt from model-host logs:```
[2026-03-15T11:12:34Z] ERROR Runtime: cudaMemcpy failed (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS)
  at kv_cache.cc:478 read_block
  device_ptr=0x7f8e3a2b, len=2048 alignment=512
  trace: launch_kernel memcpy_safe -> device_memcpy
```

tina_sre: kernel log on node-gpu-07: "nv-driver: misaligned migration pointer during unmap -> BUG: alignment fault in nv_migrate" followed by mm_faults and retry. Node shows high page reclaim activity.

olivia_support: Customer impact: spike in error rates for embeddings and ranking endpoints reported by enterprise customers. Several high-priority tickets opened referencing request ids tied to node-gpu-07. Marking as P1 for affected tenants.

orchestrator-bot: Node node-gpu-07 restart count: 5 in 6m. Pod eviction events due to OOMKilled. Scheduler reschedule attempts observed.

maya_oncall: Short mitigation: 1) cordon node-gpu-07, 2) fail traffic over to secondary pool (fallback-safe), 3) suspend cluster autoscaler, 4) reduce model shard parallelism to 1 on all hot pools. Executing cordon: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-07`

harry_runtime: Quick workaround: flip runtime flag `runtime.use_unified_migration=false` to force host-side pinned allocations for affected replicas. That should avoid pointer migration races. Also enable alignment-checker in memcpy path.

tina_sre: I've applied a taint to keep new pods off node-gpu-07 and disabled preemptive eviction on that node. Also rolled back recent driver hotpatch 525.12 -> pinned to 525.06 which was last green.

maya_oncall: Traffic shifted to fallback pool. 5xxs down ~60% in 3m, but some flaps continue on node-gpu-09 during reschedule.

harry_runtime: on a failed restart we captured this trace:```
INFO loading shard 5
WARN migration: target ptr misaligned after migration: ptr=0x7ea43af3, expected 8-byte align
ERROR cuda: illegal memory access in memcpy_atomic
Attempting to fallback to safe memcpy path with padding
```

tina_sre: hypothesis: race between background page migration (kernel/unified memory) and runtime kernel issuing direct device memcpy leading to misaligned device pointers. Triggered by aggressive autoscale/reschedule and concurrent unloads.

olivia_support: Publishing status update: "Investigating GPU-related errors impacting inference. We've shifted traffic to fallback pool and are working on a fix. We'll provide updates in 30 minutes."

eng-runtime-pager: Proposed live patch: add an alignment-safe memcpy fallback that pads unaligned copies, and gate migration/unload with device-synchronize barrier in runtime. Test in a single-staging node first. If successful, roll out to fallback pools.

maya_oncall: I've suspended the autoscaler and applied no-schedule taint to node-gpu-07/09. Also increasing warm replicas on fallback to handle load.

harry_runtime: running integration on staging-hotpool now. If tests pass, we can stage hotpatch to one production node pool and observe for 20m.

tina_sre: collecting vmcore and driver logs. If panic repeats we'll escalate to NV vendor with collected artifacts.

maya_oncall: incident timeline and actions:
- 11:10 UTC: initial OOM/illegal memory access alerts on node-gpu-07
- 11:12 UTC: auto-ticket INC-2002 created, oncall paged
- 11:15 UTC: node-gpu-07 cordoned and tainted; traffic rerouted to fallback-safe pool
- 11:18 UTC: autoscaler suspended and driver pinned to 525.06
- 11:20 UTC: alignment-safe memcpy tests started in staging

olivia_support: Noted impacted enterprise customers and initiated compensation intake process where applicable. CSMs looped in.

eng-runtime-pager: follow-ups to capture: - implement alignment-safe memcpy path and runtime migration guard - add unit/e2e synthetic test for unload+migrate race - add observability: alignment-failure counter + device pointer checksum in logs - consider throttling reschedule when page reclaim pressure > threshold

tina_sre: I'll keep continuous monitoring on node-gpu-* and will capture vmcore on any further kernel panic. Uploading artifacts to s3://incidents/INC-2002/artifacts/.

maya_oncall: Handoff in 25m. Tina, can you take lead after handoff? Keep pressure off affected nodes and coordinate hotpatch rollout.

tina_sre: Taking handoff. Will keep channel active and call bridge if hotpatch doesn't stabilize in 45m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2002 acknowledged by tina_sre. Priority: P1. Next update expected within 30 minutes.

maya_oncall: Handoff notes: cordoned nodes node-gpu-07/09; fallback routing active; autoscaler suspended; staging patch running. Logs saved under /var/log/incidents/INC-2002/.

olivia_support: Posting public update and notifying affected customers via status page and direct outreach.

eng-runtime-pager: Also bumping to-dos: add preemptive eviction throttle for runtime cgroup, blacklist affected driver version if vendor confirms, and add nightly synthetic that simulates migration/unload concurrency.
